TagDesc.Blade: Swords and knives. Classes that can equip [Blade] can use it; an attack with this tag requires an equipped [Blade].
TagDesc.Katana: Katanas. Classes that can equip [Katana] can use it; an attack with this tag requires an equipped [Katana].
TagDesc.Spear: Spears and polearms. Classes that can equip [Spear] can use it; an attack with this tag requires an equipped [Spear].
TagDesc.Hafted: Axes, maces and hammers. Classes that can equip [Hafted] can use it.
TagDesc.Staff: Staves and wands. Classes that can equip [Staff] can use it. Its Magic Power can't be combined with a [Magic Stone].
TagDesc.Bow: Bows. Classes that can equip [Bow] can use it; an attack with this tag requires an equipped [Bow].
TagDesc.Crossbow: Crossbows. Classes that can equip [Crossbow] can use it.
TagDesc.Throwing: Thrown weapons. Classes that can equip [Throwing] can use it.
TagDesc.Whip: Whips. Classes that can equip [Whip] can use it.
TagDesc.MartialArts: Fist weapons and unarmed techniques. Classes that can equip [Martial Arts] can use it.
TagDesc.MagicStone: Catalyst stones. Its Magic Power doesn't combine with a [Staff]'s nor with another Magic Stone's or Ring's: the highest counts.
TagDesc.Light: Light weapons. Classes that can equip [Light] can use it (e.g. Sorcerers can use Short Swords, but not other [Blade] items).
TagDesc.LightArmor: Light armor. Classes that can equip [Light Armor] can use it.
TagDesc.MediumArmor: Medium armor. Classes that can equip [Medium Armor] can use it.
TagDesc.HeavyArmor: Heavy armor. Classes that can equip [Heavy Armor] can use it.
TagDesc.Shield: Shields. Classes that can equip [Shield] can use it.
TagDesc.Bag: Adds Inventory Slots. A Bag with [One-Handed] or [Accessory] can also be equipped in those slots.
TagDesc.Head: Worn on the head.
TagDesc.DualWield: Requires a weapon in each hand.
TagDesc.Consumable: The item is lost when used. Unlike other actions, several Consumable items may be used in the same Process or during the Briefing.
TagDesc.Preparation: Can also be used with [Timing: Briefing] before combat without consuming the Briefing action (still only once).
TagDesc.NotForSale: Can't be bought or sold in shops.
TagDesc.Untradeable: Can't be traded to other characters.
TagDesc.Rare: Rare item, usually a prize or crafted.
TagDesc.MagicRing: Magic ring. Like a Magic Stone, its Magic Power doesn't combine with a [Staff]'s nor with another Stone's or Ring's: the highest counts.
TagDesc.SummoningWhistle: Whistle that calls a mount or companion.
TagDesc.Training: Conditioning or training. Max 2 Training skills at CR1, 3 at CR11 and 4 at CR21 (Skill Rank doesn't count).
TagDesc.Style: Fighting style. Only one [Style] skill benefits the character at a time; change it as the Setup Process action.
TagDesc.Stance: Only one [Stance] benefits the character at a time; using another ends the previous one.
TagDesc.Harmony: Bard songs. Last until the end of the Scene; by default only one Harmony active at a time, and each target only gains one of the same type.
TagDesc.ServantSummon: Druid/Summoner servants. Last until the end of the Scene; by default only one active at a time.
TagDesc.Enchantment: Enchanter skills. Last until the end of the Scene; by default only TWO active at a time.
TagDesc.Swift: Grants extra actions. At most one [Swift] action during the Briefing and during each Process.
TagDesc.Scout: Gathers information about the next Scene when used during the Briefing (only its starting state).
TagDesc.WeaponAttack: Attack made with the equipped weapon (its tags apply to the damage).
TagDesc.MeleeAttack: Requires a melee weapon; its tags apply to the damage.
TagDesc.RangedAttack: Requires a ranged weapon; its tags apply to the damage.
TagDesc.Human: A person of any of the six races.
TagDesc.Lander: A common person of the world, not an Adventurer.
TagDesc.Spell: A magic skill that doesn't attack (blessings, healing, wards). Silenced forbids it.
TagDesc.Song: A song, hymn or magic sound. Silenced forbids it.
TagDesc.Curse: Curse: the demons' power, which isn't magic. Silenced doesn't stop it, even with [Spell] or [Magic Attack].
TagDesc.Seal: A seal of the Sacred Tongue, made by a Sealer.

costs.Name: Pay Hate and Fate costs
costs.Hint: Using a skill adds its Hate cost (with the discounts of effects) and spends its Fate. Hate is only paid in a started combat; Fate always. The card shows what was paid and has an Undo button.

limits.Name: Usage limits
limits.Hint: Counts the uses of skills with a limit (1/Scene, SR/Scenario, 1/Round…) per character. A scene ends when the combat ends or with the GM tool; a scenario only with the GM tool.

actions.Name: Timing and action economy
actions.Hint: In combat, checks that a skill is used at the right time (Major, Minor, Move and Instant in your own Main Process, Setup in the Setup Process, Cleanup in the Cleanup Process) and that the Main Process action wasn't spent yet.

hatePerCombat.Name: Hate Top and Hate Under per combat
hatePerCombat.Hint: Puts [Hate Top] and [Hate Under] on the characters of every combat, so the +2 to Dodge and Hate Damage work with several combats at once, and everyone sees on the tokens who is Hate Top.

cleanup.Name: Regen and Decay in the Cleanup Process
cleanup.Hint: In the Cleanup Process of every round, Regen heals, then Decay deals damage (through Barrier). A summary is posted in the chat.

endOfProcess.Name: Statuses that end at the end of the Main Process
endOfProcess.Hint: Staggered, Dazed, Paralyzed, Silenced and Taunted end at the end of the Main Process of whoever received them. With Afflicted, the ones it protects stay.

autoApply.Name: Apply damage, healing and effects by themselves
autoApply.Hint: The damage and healing of the cards go to whoever the blow hit, and the skill's effects to whoever it reached, on the GM's window. Whoever may still use a Before Damage reaction waits for their owner. An attack without damage also counts on a failed Dodge (Hate Damage, Pursuit, Weakness, Marked).

hitDamage.Name: Damage by itself on a hit
hitDamage.Hint: When the Hit Check beats the Dodge (or the hit is automatic), the blow's damage is rolled by itself, for characters and monsters, and goes to whoever was hit through Apply damage, healing and effects by themselves. Off, a character's damage is rolled from the card's button (a monster's follows A monster's attack in one click).

monsterDamage.Name: A monster's attack in one click
monsterDamage.Hint: On the HUD, one click on the attack of a monster (or of an NPC on a hostile token) uses the skill and rolls its Check; when it hits someone, its damage is rolled at once.

monsterMinor.Name: A monster's (Minor) by itself
monsterMinor.Hint: When a monster uses an attack with (Minor) in its own turn and still has its Minor Action free, it is spent too and the bonus goes into the blow: the damage on the roll, the status on whoever it hits. The card's Undo gives it back.

monsterTarget.Name: A monster aims at the Hate Top
monsterTarget.Hint: At the start of a monster's turn, the GM's window targets the Hate Top it can reach (else the nearest). The GM changes it with a click.

autoEndTurn.Name: End of turn with the actions spent
autoEndTurn.Hint: When whoever is acting already used the Major, Minor and Move Actions: ask whether the turn ends, end it, or nothing. Who falls in their own turn also ends it (except with Do nothing).

autoPhases.Name: Setup and Cleanup by themselves
autoPhases.Hint: Setup and Cleanup go on by themselves when nobody still fighting has a skill of that phase to use (and both sides still have someone standing).

incapacitated.Name: Automatic Incapacitated
incapacitated.Hint: 0 HP (or 0 Max HP from Fatigue) makes a character Incapacitated, and an Incapacitated character drops to 0 HP. Incapacitated, Dead and Absent combatants skip their turn (straight to Post-Action).

endOfScene.Name: End of scene when the combat ends
endOfScene.Hint: When a started combat ends: Incapacitated Adventurers come back with full HP, one still Dying makes the last Death Check, Incapacitated enemies die, and Bad and Combat Statuses end. Fatigue and Weakness stay.

cards.Name: Attack and damage card fixes
cards.Hint: Damage is tied to the right attack, and the attack card gets a damage button. Apply doesn't work on a target that still has to dodge or that dodged, and asks before applying again. Private cards are shown to the owners of the targets.

autoDodge.Name: Automatic dodge for characters
autoDodge.Hint: Characters roll their Dodge Check as soon as the attack is declared, like the enemies, and the result is already on the card. Off, the character's owner rolls it from the card's Dodge button or the HUD.

closeReach.Name: Close reaches the next squares
closeReach.Hint: House rule: a Close attack also reaches a token touching the attacker's, sideways or diagonally, so the two tokens don't have to share a square. Every other range is the system's.

fate.Name: Fate buttons
fate.Hint: Spend 1 Fate to: +1d6 on a skill's Check, reroll the hit, the dodge or a plain check, and remove a Bad Status (the Fate star on the sheet). They also work for the monsters with Fate (the bosses), on the GM's window, who is asked about their [Fate 1] when they use it.

content.Name: Item and monster content
content.Hint: The trigger powers of items become skills of whoever carries them, potions and jewels heal and food removes Fatigue from whoever uses them, equipped items give their statuses at the start of the scene, and homebrew monsters get their attack damage read from their text. Only what is missing is filled; nothing edited by hand is replaced.

guideJournal.Name: Player's Guide in the Journal
guideJournal.Hint: Puts the Player's Guide in the world's Journal for everyone to read, and updates it when the system brings a new version of it (its pages become the compendium's again; the folder and permissions stay).

chatTheme.Name: Parchment chat theme
chatTheme.Hint: Skill, attack and damage cards and the rolls on parchment, with the speaker's portrait.

windowTheme.Name: Parchment system windows
windowTheme.Hint: Item and monster sheets, the effect editor, the skill and class browsers, chests and shops and the dialogs in the same look as the character sheet.

uiTheme.Name: Interface in the look of Eternia
uiTheme.Hint: The sidebar and its buttons, the Actors, Items and Journal lists, the scene controls, the players, the menus and the notifications in Eternia's green and gold. Each player chooses.

journalTheme.Name: Journals as an Eternia book
journalTheme.Hint: Journals on parchment, with the contents on the green banner, titles and text boxes as in a tabletop RPG book, also while writing a page (the editor's Eternia menu adds the boxes). Each player chooses.

iconEffects.Name: Animated icons
iconEffects.Hint: Weapon and equipment icons get a glint from level 11 and, from level 21, an aura and particles. Off, only the magic grade frames stay. Only for you.

hud.Name: Action HUD
hud.Hint: Shows a bar above the macro hotbar for the selected token: HP, Barrier, Fate, Hate and Fatigue, the checks, the skills by Timing, the items, the statuses, the turn and the pending dodges, to roll and use everything without opening the sheet. Your own setting: each player chooses.

hudCharacter.Name: HUD with no token selected
hudCharacter.Hint: With no token selected, the HUD shows the character assigned to you (players only).

turnNotice.Name: Your turn notice
turnNotice.Hint: Tells you, with a sound, when the Main Process of one of your characters starts.

turnSelect.Name: Select the token on your turn
turnSelect.Hint: When the Main Process of one of your characters starts, its token gets selected (for the GM: the enemies and NPCs no player controls).

turnPan.Name: Pan to whoever acts
turnPan.Hint: When a Main Process starts, the view goes to the acting token.

turnUntarget.Name: Clear targets at the end of your turn
turnUntarget.Hint: When the Main Process of one of your characters ends, your targets are cleared. Off (the default), a target stays until you change it.

statusLinks.Name: Clickable statuses in the chat
statusLinks.Hint: Statuses written in the cards ([Staggered], [Decay: 10], [Weakness (Flame): 5]…) become links: a click applies the status to your targets (or the selected tokens), like skill effects, until the end of the scene. Ratings with SR are worked out; missing ones are asked.

quickEffect.Name: Create an effect from a card
quickEffect.Hint: Right click a skill or item card in the chat → Create effect on targets: an effect with the skill's name, picture and text, until the end of the Process, the Round or the Scene, to track what the skill only describes in text.

hotbar.Name: Foundry macro hotbar
hotbar.Hint: Hiding the macro hotbar puts the HUD in its place; swap shows the hotbar only while the HUD is off screen (no token selected). The 1 to 0 keys keep running the macros. Your own setting: each player chooses.
hotbar.swap: Swap: shown when the HUD is gone

tokenStyle.Name: Token bars and names in the sheet's style
tokenStyle.Hint: The HP bar, Fate and the name of the tokens in the look of the sheet: the HP bar as an arc with a gold frame along the top of the ring (Fatigue hatched at its end, Barrier in a blue sliver outside), Fate as gold diamonds on the bottom edge and the name small and light right under the token, with a soft outline that reads on any map.

tokenBars.Name: Who sees the tokens' HP bar
tokenBars.Hint: For the HP bar. The second bar (Fate) follows each token's own setting.

tokenBarsCombat.Name: HP bar only in combat
tokenBarsCombat.Hint: Out of combat the HP bar and the class Motor leave the tokens; they show on the tokens in the combat.

statusAnimation.Name: Status animation on tokens
statusAnimation.Hint: A status put on a token turns into its place among the token's icons, and one taken away leaves turning, instead of the text with its name. Each player chooses.

conditionRules.Name: Automatic effects of the conditions
conditionRules.Hint: Dice, damage, turns and stacks of the conditions: Burning in the Cleanup Process, Poisoned at the start of the turn, Exposed without Defense, Last Stand, Mirror, Bond, Freezing that freezes, Fissured that breaks the guard and the other rules of the AS REGRAS journal (IX. CONDIÇÕES DA ETERNIA).

conditionLimits.Name: What the conditions forbid
conditionLimits.Hint: Actions, targets and movement the conditions forbid (Paralyzed, Silenced, Disarmed, Grappled, Taunted, Blinded…): warn asks whether to go on; block stops the players (the GM may still go on).

creationWizard.Name: Creation wizard
creationWizard.Hint: Opens the step by step creation wizard when you make a new character.

creationCard.Name: New character card
creationCard.Hint: A card in the chat when a character is made in the wizard, with its race, class, Magic and profession.

awakening.Name: The Awakening (drawn Magia)
awakening.Hint: The players' first Magia is drawn: they roll up to three times (every Magia as likely, the Ancestral and the Forbidden ones too) and keep one of what comes out, with no swap later. The GM chooses freely and may free a new draw. Off, everyone chooses their Magia.

evolutionApproval.Name: Evolving the form with the GM
evolutionApproval.Hint: On, a player's Evolve becomes a request in the chat, and the form only gives way when the GM approves. Off, the player evolves alone on reaching the stage's CR (the rite stays in the story).

dropRoll.Name: Drops: when to roll
dropRoll.Hint: When a monster's drop table rolls by itself. Whoever felled the monster gets every item and all the Yuld; what doesn't fit in the inventory stays in a loot pile on its square. Whoever came after the combat started (the summoned, the Rifts' waves) leaves nothing.
dropRoll.combat: At the end of the combat
dropRoll.manual: By hand only, from the monster sheet

marketPlayers.Name: What players see in the Market
marketPlayers.Hint: The Market button (in the token controls) lists the compendiums' items. Players only look: buying, giving and dragging from it is the GM's; they buy at the scene's shops.

Notice.Title: Eternia {version}
Notice.Body:
Eternia 1.0.1

Mounts and two new professions:

  • Mounts: the earth dragons. Buy one at the Market or a shop and ride it from the Inventory tab (section Mounts) or the Items panel of the HUD. Mounted, you run farther and get saddlebag space, and with the Wind-Repelling Blessing the Dash spends no Minor Action. In the rounds of a combat, mounting takes the Move Action; falling or being knocked prone throws you off.
  • Tamer, in the Bard's place: makes mounts at the Workshop and trains the party's (+1 Speed until the end of the scenario).
  • Sealer, in the Engineer's place: makes seals and uses Seal in combat, and the enemy loses the last skill it used until the end of the scene. On the Rifts, it writes with its Rank added.
  • Who was a Bard or an Engineer is now a Tamer or a Sealer, with the same EXP. The Songs and Gadgets you have still work.

It is all in the Player's Guide, in the chapters on equipment and professions.

StatusDesc.fatigue: [Fatigue: n] takes n from the Max HP; new Fatigue adds up. At 0 Max HP the character is Incapacitated. Food, rest or the Post-Game end it.
StatusDesc.weakness: [Weakness (Tag): n]: failing a Dodge Check against an attack with that tag (or any, without a tag) deals +n direct damage. Only the highest applies to each attack.
StatusDesc.incapacitated: At 0 HP: can't act, makes no checks and stays in Post-Action. One who isn't an enemy is [Dying] and makes Death Checks; an enemy dies at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.dead: Dead, for good: in Eternia nobody comes back from death.
StatusDesc.dying: [Dying: n]: down at death's door. In the Cleanup of every round, the Death Check: 2d6 equal to or below n kills (two 6s always hold); above it, n goes up 1. Damage on the ground raises it 2, and a critical hit kills. Any healing gets them up. With 1 Fate, roll 3d6; the Last Act trades the check for one last round.
StatusDesc.lastAct: Rose one last time: doesn't fall (stays at 1 HP), fights the whole round and dies in its Cleanup.
StatusDesc.staggered: −1d6 on Major and Main Process actions. Ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.dazed: −1d6 on Dodge Checks; can't use reaction skills (nor Obstruction). Ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.rigor: No actions with the [Movement] tag, the token doesn't move, no Obstruction. Ends with a Minor or Major Action.
StatusDesc.confused: −1d6 on every check and +1 Hate at the start of each Main Process. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.decay: [Decay: n]: n damage in the Cleanup Process. The highest Rating stays. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.pursuit: [Pursuit: n]: failing a Dodge Check deals +n direct damage and that Pursuit ends. Several stack.
StatusDesc.afflicted: Keeps Staggered, Dazed, Confused, Weakness, Overconfident, Frightened and Charmed from ending. Ends with a Minor or Major Action.
StatusDesc.overconfident: Any natural 1 on the dice is a Fumble. Ends when the character loses HP.
StatusDesc.regen: [Regen: n]: recovers n HP in the Cleanup Process. The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.cancel: [Cancel (Tag): n]: reduces damage with that tag (or any, without a tag) by n. Only the highest applies.
StatusDesc.barrier: [Barrier: n]: absorbs damage before HP, spending its Rating. The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.hidden: Others' actions can't target them (only areas). Ends on a Major Action, dealing or taking damage, being found or at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.swimming: −1d6 on every check. Puts out Burning.
StatusDesc.flying: Ignores scene objects with [Terrain]; only flyers can Obstruct them.
StatusDesc.identified: The GM reveals the enemy's defenses, Hate Multiplier and skills.
StatusDesc.standby: Delayed their Main Process: acts after everyone who isn't on Standby.
StatusDesc.hateTop: Highest Hate in the combat: takes the Hate Damage of enemy attacks.
StatusDesc.hateUnder: Hate below the Top: +2 on Dodge Checks.
StatusDesc.absent: Out of the scene: skips their turn.
StatusDesc.paralyzed: No Main Process action nor reaction, and −1d6 on Dodge Checks. Loses the turn: ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.asleep: No actions nor reactions, and fails Dodge Checks outright. Ends on taking damage, or when someone spends a Minor Action to wake them.
StatusDesc.rooted: Held to the ground: no actions with the [Movement] tag, the token doesn't move, −1d6 on Dodge Checks. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.prone: On the ground: −1d6 on their Close attacks and on Dodge Checks against Close attacks. Standing up takes the Move Action.
StatusDesc.slowed: No Move Action, and acts after everyone who isn't Slowed. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.grappled: Held by the grappler: no actions with the [Movement] tag, the token doesn't move, attacks only the grappler. Ends with a Major Action or if the grappler is Incapacitated.
StatusDesc.petrified: Turned to stone: doesn't act nor react (loses its turn), doesn't move and fails its Dodge Checks. Takes only half the damage of attacks (after Defense and Cancel). Ends at the end of its turn, the lost one (given during its own turn, at the end of the next), or when whoever petrified it is Incapacitated.
StatusDesc.silenced: No skills with the [Magic Attack], [Spell] or [Song] tags (the Curse ones still go). Ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.disarmed: No weapon attacks ([Weapon Attack], [Melee Attack], [Ranged Attack], [Sword Attack] or Range: Weapon). Taking the weapon back takes a Minor Action.
StatusDesc.blinded: −1d6 on every check but Resistance, and attacks only within 1 square. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.sealed: [Sealed (Skill)]: that skill can't be used. Without a name, it seals the last skill used. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.weakened: [Weakened: n]: −n damage on attacks. The highest Rating stays. Ends at the end of their own Main Process.
StatusDesc.amnesia: Forgot who it is: uses only Basic skills and items (a monster, only its skills without a Cost or a Limit). Ends at the end of its turn (given during its own turn, at the end of the next).
StatusDesc.frightened: −1d6 on every check against whoever frightened them, and can't move closer to them. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.charmed: Can't attack the charmer and −1d6 on Dodge Checks against them. Ends if the charmer deals them damage, or with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.taunted: Their hostile skills must target the taunter. Ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.dominated: The one who dominated them commands their body: their hostile skills can't target that one nor that one's allies (the GM plays the rest). Ends at the end of their own Main Process.
StatusDesc.berserk: [Berserk: n]: +n damage on attacks, −1d6 on Dodge Checks, and only skills that attack (and movement). Ends with a Major Action or at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.pacified: Can't hurt anyone: its attacks and spells still hit and give statuses, but deal no damage at all (not even that of a failed Dodge), and its servant doesn't hurt either. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.agony: [Agony: n]: takes n direct damage whenever it recovers HP (healing, Regen, Drain) and whenever it gets rid of a Bad Status (with an action or an effect that removes statuses). The highest Rating stays. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.nightmare: [Nightmare: n]: trapped in a nightmare, doesn't act nor react (loses its turn), doesn't move and fails its Dodge Checks; damage doesn't wake it. Takes n direct damage in the Cleanup Process. Ends at the end of its turn, the lost one (given during its own turn, at the end of the next); an ally can wake it (the GM removes it). The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.burning: [Burning: n]: n [Flame] damage in the Cleanup Process. The highest Rating stays. Ends with a Minor Action (putting it out) or when Swimming.
StatusDesc.poisoned: [Poisoned: n]: n direct damage at the start of each Main Process and −1d6 on Resistance. The highest Rating stays. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.freezing: [Freezing: n] (up to 3 stacks): −1 Speed and Initiative per stack. On the third the character freezes: Paralyzed, and the stacks clear. [Flame] damage removes them all. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.shocked: [Shocked: n]: n direct damage on every Major Action, and no reactions. The highest Rating stays. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.soaked: [Soaked: n]: +n damage from [Shock] and [Cold]. Can't be Burning (and loses it when Soaked); [Flame] damage only dries the Soaked. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.fuse: [Fuse: n]: in the Cleanup Process it goes off: n [Flame] damage, and the Fuse ends. New Fuses add to the Rating. Ends before with a Major Action (defusing).
StatusDesc.cursed: Recovers no HP (healing, Regen and items) and effects can't give them Barrier nor Regen. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.blackFlame: [Black Flame: n]: takes n [Flame] damage in the Cleanup Process and recovers no HP (healing, Regen and items don't work). Nothing puts it out: no action, water, [Soaked] or [Swimming]. The highest Rating stays. Ends at the end of the scene, when whoever lit it is Incapacitated, or with what removes Bad Statuses.
StatusDesc.exposed: The guard is down: Physical and Magic Defense are 0 and Cancel doesn't work. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.fissured: [Fissured: n] (up to 3 stacks): −2 Physical and Magic Defense per stack. On the third the guard breaks: the stacks clear, the Barrier is gone and they are Exposed. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.marked: [Marked: n]: −1d6 on Dodge Checks; failing one deals +n direct damage and the mark ends. The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.doom: [Doom: n]: the Rating drops by 1 in each Cleanup Process; at 0 the character is Incapacitated. Only what removes Bad Statuses ends it sooner.
StatusDesc.hasted: A second Minor Action in each Main Process.
StatusDesc.empowered: [Empowered: n]: +n damage on attacks. The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.focused: +1d6 on the next check (Dodge Checks included); ends after it.
StatusDesc.mirror: [Mirror: n]: when damaged by an attack, the attacker takes n direct damage.
StatusDesc.intangible: Takes no physical damage. Ends on a Major Action or in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.lastStand: When they would drop to 0 HP, they stay at 1 HP and the status ends.
StatusDesc.awakened: [Awakened: n]: the transformation. +1d6 on Accuracy checks and +n damage on attacks. When it ends, it leaves [Fatigue: n].
StatusDesc.servant: [Servant: n]: a summoned servant fights at their side. In the Cleanup Process, it strikes the nearest enemy within 4 Sq: n direct damage, with the servant's tag. The highest Rating stays. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.sun: [Sun: n] (up to 5): +n damage on attacks (or more, by the Magia) and +n to Physical and Magic Defense. In combat it rises in the Setup of each round (1, or more by the Magia) and 1 with each Sun spell. At 5 it is noon: [The One] for a round (or more), once per combat; then the Sun sets 1 per round and no longer rises. In a dark scene (night), it doesn't pass 2 (or what the Magia says). Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.theOne: Noon: takes no damage nor statuses from attacks, and its attacks deal +CR damage. Ends in the Cleanup Process (its Rating is the rounds left).
StatusDesc.counter: [Counter (Magic or Physical)]: the next attack of that type, with a single target, that hits you does nothing to you: the attacker takes double the damage you would take, as direct damage. With no type, it works against any attack, areas too. Ends after sending back a blow, or in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.grudge: [Grudge: n]: keeps the damage. Each HP you lose to attacks adds 1 (up to CR×4). A Grudge blow lets the Rating out as extra damage and clears it. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.impetus: [Impetus: n]: +n damage on attacks and +n Physical and Magic Defense. Rises by 1 at the end of each of your turns; past your CR, you lose control and become [Berserk: CR] until the Impetus ends. Ends with a Minor Action or at the end of the scene, and leaves [Fatigue: n].
StatusDesc.combo: [Combo: n]: +n damage on attacks. Each of your attacks that hits adds 1 (some spells add more). Back to 0 when you miss an attack, take damage from an attack or end a turn without attacking. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.untouchable: Takes no magic damage (the pair of Intangible, which takes no physical damage). Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.inversion: The magic damage it would take (after Defense and Cancel) heals it instead. In turn, the healing it gets hurts, and the effects that would give it [Empowered] or [Regen] give [Weakened] or [Decay] with the same Rating. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.rhythm: [Rhythm: n] (up to 3): the next damage of one of your spells (or of a [Magic Attack] or [Spell]) adds +n d6, and the Rhythm ends. New Rhythms add up. Also ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.clones: [Clones: n] (up to 6): when an attack would hit you, roll 1d6: up to n, it hits a copy (nothing reaches you, no damage nor statuses) and the Clones go down by 1. Your Close attacks deal +n damage. New Clones add up. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.bond: Half the HP damage they would take goes to whoever made the Bond, as direct damage. Ends at the end of the scene or if that character is Incapacitated.
StatusDesc.contagion: [Contagion: n]: takes n direct damage in the Cleanup and passes [Contagion: n] to the allies within 1 square that don't have it yet (whoever caught it only hurts and spreads from the next Cleanup). The highest Rating stays. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.reaped: [Sealed Life: n]: a death god sealed n of your Max HP, and it doesn't come back: not with healing, not at the end of the scene, not with rest. Only when whoever sealed it dies for good (or when the Reaper is paid, for the caster's own price).
StatusDesc.ironBlood: [Iron Blood: n] (up to 5): the iron of your blood turned into blades. Every square you move on your own costs n direct damage (being pulled, pushed or switched doesn't count). At 5, the iron leaves the blood at once: [Dazed] and [Slowed]. Ends with a Major Action or at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.phasing: You go through everything: no attack reaches you (neither damage nor statuses), and each one that passes gives +1 [Anticipation]. In exchange you attack no one and use no skill against others (only those made for it). Given on your turn, it lasts until the end of your next turn.
StatusDesc.anticipation: [Anticipation: n] (up to 5): the blows that passed through you, kept. The blow that comes back (the spells of Permeation) spends it all and adds it to the damage. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.erased: Your magic was erased: you use no spells (not even Curses, which [Silenced] lets by), and the Traits of your Magias stop. Ends in the Cleanup.
StatusDesc.gaze: The eyes without the blindfold: when it comes and in every Setup, everyone within 4 Sq of you (allies too, not you) is [Erased]. Each Cleanup with them open gives [Fatigue: 1]; they close by themselves after 3 rounds, or with a Minor Action (Break Free).
StatusDesc.hourglass: [Hourglass: n] (up to 3): the time you turned back. Full, the next Rewind overflows: it turns back the time of everyone within 3 Sq (enemies too), you fall [Asleep] and the hourglass empties.
StatusDesc.jackpot: [Jackpot: n]: the prize. You get all your HP back now and in every Setup, you don't fall (at 0 HP you come back with full HP), your spells cost no Hate and your attacks deal +CR damage. The Rating is the rounds left: it drops 1 in every Cleanup.
StatusDesc.luck: [Luck: n] (up to 3): the pairs the reels gave. At 3, the [Jackpot] (and the Luck goes to 0). Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.goliath: [Goliath: n]: the giant's body. A blow whose damage (after the Defense and Cancel) is below n does nothing, not even its statuses; n or more passes whole. You aren't pulled, pushed nor switched, and your physical attacks deal +CR damage. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.quake: [Quake: n] (up to 5): the quakes you made so far. Each point makes the next spells of the Cataclismo stronger. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.mounted: On a mount: its Speed, space, Initiative and Defenses count, and its powers can be used. Falling, dying or being knocked [Prone] throws the rider off.

banquet.text: Turn 2 equal foods into one portion for the whole party: every player character eats.

copy.name: Copy
copy.text: Write one of your skills on a scroll anyone uses once, with your Skill Rank, check and damage. Spends an attempt and gives 2 EXP.

gather.name: Gathering
gather.text: Roll 2d6 + Rank: 8 or more finds 1 Anima-mundi of the level you choose (up to your CR), 11 or more finds 2, and two sixes also find a Quintessence. What you find has no Seal of the Anima: it serves in the Workshop, but no shop buys it. Spends an attempt.

retouch.name: Retouch
retouch.text: Swap one enhancement of a crafted item for another of its list: it costs 2 Anima-mundi of the item's level (100 Yuld at Level 1), doubling with each retouch of the item. Spends an attempt and gives 5 EXP. You sell everything at full price, but not the Anima-mundi without the Seal of the Anima, which nobody buys.

train.name: Train
train.text: In the Interlude, a mount of a character of the party gets +1 Speed until the end of its owner's scenario. Spends an attempt.
train.effect: +{n} Speed until the end of the scenario, while ridden (trained by {name}).

seal.name: Seal
seal.text: In combat, the skill Seal (Major Action, up to 4 Sq): Accuracy + Rank against an enemy's Resistance; on a hit it is [Sealed] (the last skill it used) until the end of the scene. Spends an attempt and gives 2 EXP. On the Rifts, your writing adds your Rank.

Why.potent: This item doesn't heal, deal damage, remove Fatigue or give a rated status.
Why.quick: Only for Major Action or Rest Time items.
Why.wide: Only for Self, Single or numbered targets.
Why.hostile: Only for items used on allies.

Copy.Name: Scroll: {name}

Banquet.Name: Banquet: {name}

Hint.fusion: Two equal crafted items (same base and quality) become one of the next quality, with one more enhancement. Spends no attempt.
Hint.gather: Choose the level of the Anima-mundi you look for (up to your CR) and roll 2d6 + Rank.
Hint.retouch: Choose an item made in a Workshop to swap one enhancement.
Hint.sell: You sell at full price. Magic items give 2 EXP.

Hint.banquet: Two equal foods become one portion for the whole party.
Hint.copy: Choose one of your skills. Spends an attempt and gives 2 EXP.
Hint.train: Choose a mount of the party. Spends an attempt.

Bench.EmptyCatalog: No catalog item for this profession.
Bench.EmptyInventory: No item in the bag this profession makes. See the catalog.
Bench.EmptyFusion: No pair of equal crafted items.
Bench.EmptyRetouch: No item made in a Workshop in the bag.

Lede.fusion: The enhancements of one of the items stay; choose one more.

Reveal.salvage: Nothing came out, but the Anima-mundi {n} is back.

Issue.Weapon: Needs a {tags} weapon in the main hand.

Motor.Choose: How many {unit} to spend? You have {have}.

Samurai.Name: Sheath
Samurai.FullMoonIssue: Full Moon Path: the Iai only with a full Sheath ({n} Cuts).

Card.Gain: In the Setup Process, with the blade sheathed: +1 Cut.
Card.Spend: The Iai (Initiative, spends the Major Action) draws and spends them all: each Cut adds 1d6 + CR÷2 to the damage.
Card.Cap: 2 Cuts, +1 every 5 CR. With a full Sheath, a Perfect Cut: automatic hit; the first one of the scene adds +[CR×2+10].
Card.Reset: Any other weapon attack draws the blade and loses the Cuts. Sheathing is a Minor Action.
Card.GainLesser: In the Setup Process, with the blade sheathed: +1 Cut.
Card.SpendLesser: The Iai draws and spends them all: each Cut adds 1d6 + CR÷2 to the damage, without a Perfect Cut.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Sheath's cap, at least 1.
Card.ResetLesser: Any other weapon attack draws the blade and loses the Cuts.

Motor.CardActionFailed: The Motor action failed; see the console (F12).

Assassino.Name: Contract
Assassino.OneTarget: Target a single enemy to swear the Contract.
Assassino.EnemyTarget: The Contract can only be sworn on an enemy.
Assassino.NotTarget: The Execution only works on the Contract's Target ({name}): target it.
Assassino.FullIssue: Executioner's Path: the Execution needs a full Contract ({n} Breaches).
Assassino.Executed: {name} falls: the Execution drops anyone at {n} HP or less.

Card.Gain: Any hit anyone lands on the Target: +1 Breach (your Stab: +2).
Card.Spend: The Execution, only on the Target, spends them all: each Breach adds 1d6 + CR. A Target left at HP ≤ [Breaches × (CR+5)] falls (not a [Boss]).
Card.Cap: 3 Breaches, +1 every 5 CR. With a full Contract, the Execution hits without a Dodge Check.
Card.Reset: Swearing a Contract on another Target loses the Breaches. The Target falling fulfills the Contract: you are free.
Card.GainLesser: Any hit anyone lands on the Target: +1 Breach.
Card.SpendLesser: The Execution, only on the Target, spends them all: each Breach adds 1d6 + CR, without the fall.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Contract's cap, at least 1.
Card.ResetLesser: Swearing a Contract on another Target loses the Breaches. The Target falling fulfills the Contract.

Berserker.Name: Rage
Berserker.BleedIssue: Bleed costs {n} HP: you need more HP than that.

Card.Gain: +1 Rage every time an enemy attack takes HP from you; +1 more at half your HP or less.
Card.Spend: Savage Strike spends it all: (1+Rage)d6 + Rage×CR. Breath of Blood turns Rage into HP.
Card.Cap: 3 Rage, +1 every 5 CR. With Rage, weapon attacks add +[Rage] to the damage.
Card.Reset: At the Cleanup Process of a round in which you neither attacked nor lost HP, lose 1 Rage.
Card.GainLesser: +1 Rage every time an enemy attack takes HP from you.
Card.SpendLesser: Savage Strike spends it all: (1+Rage)d6 + Rage×CR.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Rage cap, at least 1. With Rage, weapon attacks add +[Rage] to the damage.
Card.ResetLesser: At the Cleanup Process of a round in which you neither attacked nor lost HP, lose 1 Rage.

Card.Gain: In the Setup Process, if the token didn't move in the round before: +1. Steady Aim (Move Action): +1.
Card.Spend: Sure Shot spends all the Aim: each point adds 1d6 + CR to the damage.
Card.Cap: 3, +1 every 5 CR. With a full Aim, the Sure Shot's target is [Exposed].
Card.Reset: Moving the token loses all the Aim.
Card.GainLesser: Steady Aim (Move Action): +1. Nothing in the Setup Process.
Card.SpendLesser: Sure Shot spends all the Aim: each point adds 1d6 + CR to the damage, without [Exposed].
Card.CapLesser: Half the cap of Aim, at least 1.
Card.ResetLesser: Moving the token loses all the Aim.

Comandante.Name: Tactics

Card.Gain: In the Setup Process: +1 Order. Survey the Field (Minor Action): +1.
Card.Spend: Each Order makes an ally act out of turn: Order: Attack! (a basic attack now, with [Focused]) and Order: Advance! (move now, with [Barrier]).
Card.Cap: 2 Orders, +1 every 5 CR.
Card.Reset: At the end of the combat.
Card.GainLesser: Survey the Field (Minor Action): +1. Nothing in the Setup Process.
Card.SpendLesser: Order: Attack!: an ally makes a basic attack now, with [Focused].
Card.CapLesser: 1 Order.
Card.ResetLesser: At the end of the combat.

Comandante.MarshalIssue: Marshal: an Order for two allies spends 2 Orders.

Druida.Name: Forms

Card.Gain: At the Setup, in the human form: +1 Sap. Earth Sap also gives +1.
Card.Spend: The Call of the Beast spends 1 Sap to become a beast; as a beast, each Cleanup costs 1, and with no Sap you go back to the human form.
Card.Cap: 3 Sap, +1 every 5 CR. Bear: [Cancel: 2 + Sap]. Wolf: [Empowered: CR÷2 + 2].
Card.Reset: Every combat starts in the human form, with 1 Sap.
Card.GainLesser: At the Setup, in the human form: +1 Sap.
Card.SpendLesser: The Call of the Beast spends 1 Sap to become a wolf; as a beast, each Cleanup costs 1.
Card.CapLesser: Half the cap of the Forms, at least 1. Only the wolf form.
Card.ResetLesser: Every combat starts in the human form, with 1 Sap.

Druida.AlreadyBear: You are already in the bear form.
Druida.NoBear: The Lesser Forms have no bear form.

Estrategista.Name: Reading

Card.Gain: Study the Field, at the Setup Process: roll 2d6 and keep both dice as a Reading.
Card.Spend: On the attack cards, a Reading replaces the two lowest dice of one of your checks; other skills spend a Reading for its sum.
Card.Cap: 1 Reading, +1 every 5 CR. Over the cap, you choose which to drop.
Card.Reset: At the end of the combat.
Card.GainLesser: Study the Field, at the Setup Process: roll 2d6 and keep both dice as a Reading.
Card.SpendLesser: On the attack cards, a Reading replaces the two lowest dice of one of your checks.
Card.CapLesser: 1 Reading.
Card.ResetLesser: At the end of the combat.

Estrategista.Keep: Choose the two dice the Reading keeps.
Estrategista.Discard: Readings over the cap: choose which to drop.
Estrategista.ReviseHint: Which Reading do you revise? Its lowest die is rolled again.
Estrategista.ChooseOptional: Spend a Reading? With it, the target is also [Marked].
Estrategista.OwnTip: Replaces the two lowest dice of the check with {a} and {b}; the Reading is gone.
Estrategista.EnemyTip: Replaces the two highest dice of the check with {a} and {b}; the Reading is gone.
Estrategista.MaxSum: Needs a Reading that adds up to {n} or less.
Estrategista.MinSum: Needs a Reading that adds up to {n} or more.
Estrategista.Kept: {name}: the Reading {a}+{b} worked and comes back (Chess Path).
Estrategista.Deduction: {name} plays the Reading {a}+{b} on "{test}": the total becomes {total}.
Estrategista.NoCheck: No check of yours to change: roll the check first.

Feiticeiro.Name: Heat

Card.Gain: +1 Heat per Spell of the class (the big ones, +2). Your Spells add +[Heat × 2] to their damage.
Card.Spend: The Eruption (area, needs 2) lets all the Heat out: each point adds 1d6 + CR. Breathe the Flame lets 2 out.
Card.Cap: 3 Heat, +1 every 5 CR. At the cap, Incandescent: Overload at the Cleanup ([Heat × CR] direct damage).
Card.Reset: The Eruption empties the Heat; so does the end of the combat.
Card.GainLesser: +1 Heat per Spell of the class. Your Spells add +[Heat] to their damage.
Card.SpendLesser: The Eruption (needs 2) lets all the Heat out: each point adds 1d6 + CR.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Heat cap, at least 1. At the cap, Incandescent and Overload at the Cleanup.
Card.ResetLesser: The Eruption empties the Heat; so does the end of the combat.

Feiticeiro.ChooseEruption: How much Heat does the Eruption spend? You have {have}.

Guardiao.Name: Bulwark
Guardiao.WardIssue: Target one ally to be your Ward.

Card.Gain: +1 Layer every time an enemy makes an attack against you, hit or miss.
Card.Spend: The Bulwark Strike spends them all: (1 + Layers)d6 + Attack Power, and the target is [Taunted].
Card.Cap: 3 Layers, +1 every 5 CR. In combat, each Layer is [Cancel: 1].
Card.Reset: At the Cleanup Process of a round in which no enemy attacked you, lose 1 Layer.
Card.GainLesser: +1 Layer every time an enemy makes an attack against you, hit or miss.
Card.SpendLesser: The Bulwark Strike spends them all: (1 + Layers)d6 + Attack Power.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Bulwark's cap, at least 1. In combat, each Layer is [Cancel: 1].
Card.ResetLesser: At the Cleanup Process of a round in which no enemy attacked you, lose 1 Layer.

Invocador.Name: Pact

Card.Gain: Summon Spirit: choose the Wolf, the Golem or the Fairy and pay [CR÷2+2] HP per Link. With a spirit there, the spells of the Magias give +1 Link (the big ones, +2).
Card.Spend: The special commands spend Links; the Living Shield spends 1. Command: Attack rolls 1d6 more per Link. The supreme spells need the cap and spend them all, with a spirit that came before this round.
Card.Cap: 3 Links, +1 every 5 CR. Wolf: +1d6 to its strikes; Golem: [Cancel: Links]; Fairy: [Regen: Links × 2].
Card.Reset: With 0 Links the spirit fades. Every combat starts without a spirit.
Card.GainLesser: Summon Spirit, the Wolf only: [CR÷2+2] HP per Link.
Card.SpendLesser: Command: Attack rolls 1d6 more per Link, and the Wolf adds +1d6.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Pact's cap, at least 1.
Card.ResetLesser: With 0 Links the Wolf fades. Every combat starts without a spirit.

Invocador.NoHp: Too few HP: each Link costs {cost} HP, and you must keep at least 1.
Invocador.Full: The Pact is already at its cap.
Invocador.NoSwap: There is only one spirit to call.
Invocador.SupremeWait: The spirit came this round: the supreme spell waits for the next one.
Invocador.ChooseLinks: How many Links? Each costs {cost} HP (you have {hp}).
Invocador.Returned: {name} recovers {hp} HP: the spirit went back to the void.

Menestrel.Name: Movements

Card.Gain: At the Setup Process, still singing the same song: +1 Movement.
Card.Spend: The Finale (Major) spends them all on a burst of the song until the end of the round, and you fall silent.
Card.Cap: 3 Movements, +1 at CR 10. The song is on you and your allies in the combat (the Lament, on the enemies).
Card.Reset: Starting or changing a song (Minor) goes back to Movement I. [Silenced] at the Setup Process, the song stops.
Card.GainLesser: At the Setup Process, still singing the same song: +1 Movement.
Card.SpendLesser: The Finale spends them all on a burst of the song until the end of the round.
Card.CapLesser: 2 Movements.
Card.ResetLesser: Changing songs goes back to Movement I. [Silenced] at the Setup Process, the song stops.

Menestrel.SameSong: You are already singing that song.

Monge.Name: Chain
Monge.WeaponIssue: The Chain strikes need a [Martial Arts] weapon in the main hand or both hands empty.

Card.Gain: Opening Strike and Quick Link: +1 Link each.
Card.Spend: The Final Strike spends them all: (1 + Links)d6 + Links×CR. With a full Chain, the target is [Dazed].
Card.Cap: 3 Links, +1 every 5 CR.
Card.Reset: A turn without a Chain skill breaks it. Each enemy attack that takes your HP takes 1 Link.
Card.GainLesser: Opening Strike: +1 Link.
Card.SpendLesser: The Final Strike spends them all: (1 + Links)d6 + Links×CR, without the full Chain's effect.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Chain's cap, at least 1.
Card.ResetLesser: A turn without a Chain skill breaks it. Each enemy attack that takes your HP takes 1 Link.

Card.Gain: +1 Burden per miracle (the big ones, +2). The miracles add +[Burden × 2] to their healing or damage.
Card.Spend: The Revelation (area, needs 2) lets all the Burden out: it heals [(Burden)d6 + Recovery + Burden×CR]. Penance takes 1 away.
Card.Cap: 4 Burden, +1 every 5 CR. From 3 on, [Weakness: Burden × 2]; at the cap, also [Cursed].
Card.Reset: The Revelation empties the Burden; so does the end of the combat.
Card.GainLesser: +1 Burden per miracle. The miracles add +[Burden] to their healing or damage.
Card.SpendLesser: The Revelation (needs 2) lets all the Burden out.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Burden cap, at least 1. At the cap, [Cursed]; no [Weakness].
Card.ResetLesser: The Revelation empties the Burden; so does the end of the combat.

Ressonante.Name: Spark

Card.Gain: At the Setup: +1 Glow. Resonant Strike, with the Spark in the weapon: +1.
Card.Spend: Leap the Spark: the old piece releases its Awakening, and the new one starts with half the Glow.
Card.Cap: 3 Glow, +1 every 5 CR. Weapon: +[Glow × 2] damage. Armor: [Cancel: Glow × 2]. Jewel: +[Glow × 2] to magic and healing.
Card.Reset: Every combat starts with the Spark in the weapon and 0 Glow.
Card.GainLesser: At the Setup: +1 Glow. Resonant Strike, with the Spark in the weapon: +1.
Card.SpendLesser: Leap the Spark between the weapon and the armor: the old piece releases its Awakening.
Card.CapLesser: Half the cap of the Spark, at least 1. Only the weapon and the armor.
Card.ResetLesser: Every combat starts with the Spark in the weapon and 0 Glow.

Ressonante.ChooseSlot: Which piece does the Spark leap to? It has {n} Glow.
Ressonante.IconLocked: Single Icon Path: the Spark doesn't leap in combat.

Sacerdote.Name: Grace

Card.Gain: Each enemy attack that takes HP from an ally: +1 Grace (+1 if they are left at half HP or less).
Card.Spend: Healing Prayer and Shield of Faith spend as much Grace as you want: heal after or protect before.
Card.Cap: 3 Grace, +1 every 5 CR.
Card.Reset: At the end of the combat. Every combat starts at 0.
Card.GainLesser: Each enemy attack that takes HP from an ally: +1 Grace.
Card.SpendLesser: Healing Prayer and Shield of Faith spend as much Grace as you want.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Grace cap, at least 1.
Card.ResetLesser: At the end of the combat.

Sacerdote.Pick: How much Grace to spend? You have {have}.

Tecelao.Name: Pattern

Card.Gain: A check of anyone in the combat with two dice that add up to the Pattern: +1 Thread (6 to 8), +2 (4, 5, 9, 10) or +3 (2, 3, 11, 12).
Card.Spend: On the attack cards, 1 Thread: the lowest die of a check goes up by 1 or the highest goes down by 1 (2 Threads when that makes or unmakes a Critical or a Fumble).
Card.Cap: 3 Threads, +1 every 5 CR. The Pattern, a number from 2 to 12, is chosen at the Setup Process.
Card.Reset: At the end of the combat. Changing the Pattern in the middle of a combat loses the Threads.
Card.GainLesser: A check of anyone in the combat with two dice that add up to the Pattern: +1 Thread (6 to 8), +2 (4, 5, 9, 10) or +3 (2, 3, 11, 12).
Card.SpendLesser: On the attack cards, 1 Thread: the lowest die of a check goes up by 1 (2 Threads when that makes a Critical or unmakes a Fumble).
Card.CapLesser: Half the Pattern's cap, at least 1.
Card.ResetLesser: At the end of the combat. Changing the Pattern in the middle of a combat loses the Threads.

Tecelao.ChooseHint: The Pattern: the number two dice of a check must add up to. The rare ones give more Threads.
Tecelao.ChooseSecond: The second number of the Pattern.
Tecelao.ChanceIssue: Path of Chance: the Pattern is rolled at the Setup Process.
Tecelao.ChanceFlavor: Path of Chance: the Pattern of the round
Tecelao.KnotHint: How many Threads does the Lasso tighten? Each adds +1d6 to the damage; with at least 1, the target is also [Rooted].
Tecelao.UpTip: 1 Thread: the lowest die of the check goes up by 1. Costs 2 when it makes or unmakes a Critical or a Fumble.
Tecelao.DownTip: 1 Thread: the highest die of the check goes down by 1. Costs 2 when it makes or unmakes a Critical or a Fumble.
Tecelao.SixTip: 1 Thread: the lowest die of the check becomes 6. Costs 2 when it makes a Critical or unmakes a Fumble.
Tecelao.OneTip: 1 Thread: the highest die of the check becomes 1. Costs 2 when it makes a Fumble or unmakes a Critical.
Tecelao.FateTip: Every Thread (at least 3): the check becomes a Fumble. Once per combat.
Tecelao.NoDie: No die of that check can change that way.

Matador.Name: Scales

Card.Gain: Devour: +1 (+2 with a source of your element). Dragon's Iron Fist: +1. An attack of your element that strikes you: +1.
Card.Spend: The dragon moves: the Roar, the Claw, the Wing and the others.
Card.Cap: 3 Scales, +1 every 5 CR. At the cap, the Dragon Force: [Awakened: CR + 2×Seed] and −1 Scale at the Cleanup, until none are left.
Card.Reset: The end of the combat empties the Scales. When the Force ends it leaves [Fatigue] and the Seed grows by 1 (it empties at the end of the scenario).
Card.GainLesser: Devour: +1 (+2 with a source of your element). Dragon's Iron Fist: +1. An attack of your element that strikes you: +1.
Card.SpendLesser: The dragon moves.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Scales cap, at least 1. No Dragon Force.
Card.ResetLesser: The end of the combat empties the Scales.

Matador.Eats: eats the attack of its element, no damage
Matador.InnerDragon: The inner dragon of {name} wakes up: the Scales fill and the Dragon Force comes.

Hint.ceu: Is there air within your reach? The GM confirms.
Hint.raio: Is there lightning within your reach (a storm, a lightning lacrima, a generator)? The GM confirms.

Hint.sombras: Is there shadow within your reach (the night, a dark hall, the shadow of a wall)? The GM confirms.
Hint.veneno: Is there poison within your reach (a swamp, a cloud of gas, a vial, a snake)? The GM confirms.

Issue.InForce: You are already in the Dragon Force.
Issue.Half: Needs {n} Scales (half the cap); you have {have}.

Chips.seed: Dragon Seed: how many Dragon Forces already ended this scenario

MagoAzul.Name: Souls

Card.Gain: Every Spell, the class's or the Magias', +1 Essence (the big ones, +2); absorbing a soul, +1; in a form, +1 at each Setup Process.
Card.Spend: The Soul Strike spends all the Essence and leaves the nature's mark. The supreme spells need the cap and spend it all.
Card.Cap: 3 Essence, +1 every 5 CR. The grimoire keeps 3 souls (+1 every 5 CR) besides the First.
Card.Reset: At the end of the combat, the Essence and the form. The grimoire stays.
Card.GainLesser: Absorb gives +1 Essence (and +1 when it absorbs a soul); in a form, +1 at each Setup Process.
Card.SpendLesser: The Dedication talents spend the Essence. The grimoire keeps 1 soul besides the First.
Card.CapLesser: Half the cap of the Souls, at least 1.
Card.ResetLesser: At the end of the combat, the Essence and the form. The grimoire stays.

MagoAzul.ChooseFirst: The First Soul's nature, for good: Beast (Strength), Animal (Dexterity), Demon (Power) or Spirit (Intelligence).
MagoAzul.WholeLock: Whole Body: the soul only leaves with the Essence at the cap.
MagoAzul.NoSouls: No absorbed soul in the grimoire.
MagoAzul.NeedsSoul: Wear an absorbed soul (not the First).
MagoAzul.FeastHint: The soul you let go of (it is gone).
MagoAzul.Replaced: The soul of {soul} left the grimoire.
MagoAzul.Escaped: The soul of {soul} escaped: the grimoire's are stronger.

MagoBranco.Name: Law

Card.Gain: A check of anyone in the combat with two dice that add up to the Law: +1 Rune (6 to 8), +2 (4, 5, 9, 10) or +3 (2, 3, 11, 12), at most 2 a round. Every Spell, the class's or the Magias', lights +1 (the big ones, +2).
